1.english_reference: Behold , the hope of him is in vain

traditions.KJV: Behold , the hope of him is in vain :

1.english_reference: shall not [ one ] be cast down even at the sight of him ?

traditions.WLC: הֲ גַ֖ם אֶל מַרְאָ֣י ו יֻטָֽל
traditions.LXX: οὐδὲ ἐπὶ τοῖς λεγομένοις τεθαύμακας ; οὐδὲ δέδοικας ὅτι ἡτοίμασταί μοι ;
traditions.KJV: shall not [ one ] be cast down even at the sight of him ?

2.english_reference: None [ is so ] fierce that dare stir him up

traditions.KJV: None [ is so ] fierce that dare stir him up :

2.english_reference: who then is able to stand before me ?

traditions.WLC: נּוּ וּ מִ֥י ה֝֗וּא לְ פָנַ֥ י יִתְיַצָּֽב
traditions.LXX: τίς γάρ ἐστιν ὁ ἐμοὶ ἀντιστάς ; ἢ τίς ἀντιστήσεταί μοι καὶ ὑπομενεῖ ; εἰ πᾶσα ἡ ὑπ᾽ οὐρανὸν ἐμή ἐστιν ,
traditions.VUL: quis enim resístere potest vúltui meo ?
traditions.KJV: who then is able to stand before me ?

3.english_reference: Who hath prevented me , that I should repay [ him ?

traditions.LXX: οὐ σιωπήσομαι δι᾽ αὐτόν , καὶ λόγον δυνάμεως ἐλεήσει τὸν ἴσον αὐτοῦ .
traditions.VUL: Quis ante dedit mihi , ut reddam ei ?
traditions.KJV: Who hath prevented me , that I should repay [ him ?

3.english_reference: whatsoever is under the whole heaven is mine .

traditions.WLC: תַּ֖חַת כָּל הַ שָּׁמַ֣יִם לִ י הֽוּא
traditions.VUL: ómnia quæ sub cælo sunt , mea sunt .
traditions.KJV: whatsoever is ] under the whole heaven is mine .

4.english_reference: I will not conceal his parts ,

traditions.KJV: I will not conceal his parts ,

traditions.LXX: εἰς δὲ πτύξιν θώρακος αὐτοῦ τίς ἂν εἰσέλθοι ;
traditions.KJV: nor his power ,
nor his comely proportion .

5.english_reference: Who can discover the face of his garment ?

traditions.KJV: Who can discover the face of his garment ? [ or ]

5.english_reference: [ or ] who can come [ to him ] with his double bridle ?

traditions.WLC: בְּ כֶ֥פֶל רִ֝סְנ֗ וֹ מִ֣י יָבֽוֹא
traditions.VUL: et in médium oris eius quis intrábit ?
traditions.KJV: who can come [ to him ] with his double bridle ?

6.english_reference: Who can open the doors of his face ?

traditions.LXX: τὰ ἔγκατα αὐτοῦ ἀσπίδες χάλκειαι , σύνδεσμος αὐτοῦ ὥσπερ σμιρίτης λίθος ·
traditions.KJV: Who can open the doors of his face ?

6.english_reference: his teeth [ are ] terrible round about .

traditions.KJV: his teeth [ are ] terrible round about .
[ His ] scales [ are his ] pride ,

7.english_reference: shut up together [ as with ] a close seal .

traditions.LXX: πνεῦμα δὲ οὐ μὴ διέλθῃ αὐτόν ·
traditions.KJV: shut up together [ as with ] a close seal .

8.english_reference: One is so near to another ,

traditions.KJV: One is so near to another ,

8.english_reference: that no air can come between them .

traditions.WLC: וְ֝ ר֗וּחַ לֹא יָב֥וֹא בֵֽינֵי הֶֽם
traditions.VUL: et ne spiráculum quidem incédit per eas :
traditions.KJV: that no air can come between them .

9.english_reference: They are joined one to another ,

traditions.KJV: They are joined one to another ,

traditions.LXX: οἱ δὲ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ εἶδος ἑωσφόρου .
traditions.KJV: they stick together ,

9.english_reference: that they can not be sundered .

traditions.KJV: that they can not be sundered .

10.english_reference: By his neesings a light doth shine ,

traditions.LXX: ἐκ στόματος αὐτοῦ ἐκπορεύονται λαμπάδες καιόμεναι ,
traditions.KJV: By his neesings a light doth shine ,

10.english_reference: and his eyes [ are ] like the eyelids of the morning .

traditions.WLC: וְ֝ עֵינָ֗י ו כְּ עַפְעַפֵּי שָֽׁחַר
traditions.VUL: et óculi eius , ut pálpebræ dilúculi .
traditions.KJV: and his eyes [ are ] like the eyelids of the morning .

11.english_reference: Out of his mouth go burning lamps

traditions.LXX: ἐκ μυκτήρων αὐτοῦ ἐκπορεύεται καπνὸς καμίνου καιομένης πυρὶ ἀνθράκων ·
traditions.KJV: Out of his mouth go burning lamps , [ and ]
sparks of fire leap out .

12.english_reference: Out of his nostrils goeth smoke

traditions.KJV: Out of his nostrils goeth smoke ,

12.english_reference: as out of a seething pot or caldron

traditions.LXX: φλὸξ δὲ ἐκ στόματος αὐτοῦ ἐκπορεύεται .
traditions.KJV: as [ out ] of a seething pot or caldron .

traditions.LXX: ἐν δὲ τραχήλῳ αὐτοῦ αὐλίζεται δύναμις ,
traditions.KJV: His breath kindleth coals ,

13.english_reference: and a flame goeth out of his mouth

traditions.WLC: וְ֝ לַ֗הַב מִ פִּ֥י ו יֵצֵֽא
traditions.VUL: et flamma de ore eius egréditur .
traditions.KJV: and a flame goeth out of his mouth .
In his neck remaineth strength ,

14.english_reference: and sorrow is turned into joy before him

traditions.WLC: וּ֝ לְ פָנָ֗י ו תָּד֥וּץ דְּאָבָֽה
traditions.KJV: and sorrow is turned into joy before him .

15.english_reference: The flakes of his flesh are joined together

traditions.LXX: ἡ καρδία αὐτοῦ πέπηγεν ὡς λίθος ,
traditions.KJV: The flakes of his flesh are joined together :
they are firm in themselves ;

traditions.VUL: et ad locum álium non feréntur .
traditions.KJV: they can not be moved .

16.english_reference: His heart is as firm as a stone ;

traditions.KJV: His heart is as firm as a stone ;

16.english_reference: yea , as hard as a piece of the nether [ millstone ] .

traditions.KJV: yea , as hard as a piece of the nether [ millstone ] .

17.english_reference: When he raiseth up himself, the mighty are afraid

traditions.LXX: ἐὰν συναντήσωσιν αὐτῷ λόγχαι , οὐδὲν μὴ ποιήσωσιν δόρυ καὶ θώρακα ·
traditions.KJV: When he raiseth up himself , the mighty are afraid :

17.english_reference: by reason of breakings they purify themselves

traditions.KJV: by reason of breakings they purify themselves .

18.english_reference: The sword of him that layeth at him can not hold

traditions.VUL: Cum apprehénderit eum gládius , subsístere non póterit
traditions.KJV: The sword of him that layeth at him can not hold :

18.english_reference: the spear, the dart, nor the habergeon

traditions.KJV: the spear , the dart , nor the habergeon .

traditions.LXX: οὐ μὴ τρώσῃ αὐτὸν τόξον χάλκειον · ἥγηται μὲν πετροβόλον χόρτον ,
traditions.KJV: He esteemeth iron as straw , [
and ] brass as rotten wood .

20.english_reference: The arrow can not make him flee

traditions.KJV: The arrow can not make him flee :

20.english_reference: slingstones are turned with him into stubble

traditions.WLC: לְ֝ קַ֗שׁ נֶהְפְּכוּ ל֥ וֹ אַבְנֵי קָֽלַע
traditions.VUL: in stípulam versi sunt ei lápides fundæ .
traditions.KJV: slingstones are turned with him into stubble .

traditions.LXX: πᾶς δὲ χρυσὸς θαλάσσης ὑπ᾽ αὐτὸν ὥσπερ πηλὸς ἀμύθητος .
traditions.KJV: he laugheth at the shaking of a spear .
Sharp stones [ are ] under him :

traditions.LXX: ἥγηται δὲ τὴν θάλασσαν ὥσπερ ἐξάλιπτρον ,
traditions.VUL: et sternet sibi aurum quasi lutum .
traditions.KJV: he spreadeth sharp pointed things upon the mire .

23.english_reference: He maketh the deep to boil like a pot

traditions.LXX: τὸν δὲ τάρταρον τῆς ἀβύσσου ὥσπερ αἰχμάλωτον ·
traditions.VUL: Fervéscere fáciet quasi ollam profúndum mare ,
traditions.KJV: He maketh the deep to boil like a pot :

23.english_reference: he maketh the sea like a pot of ointment

traditions.VUL: et ponet quasi cum unguénta búlliunt .
traditions.KJV: he maketh the sea like a pot of ointment .

24.english_reference: He maketh a path to shine after him

traditions.LXX: οὐκ ἔστιν οὐδὲν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ὅμοιον αὐτῷ ,
traditions.KJV: He maketh a path to shine after him ; [

traditions.LXX: πεποιημένον ἐνκαταπαίζεσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀγγέλων μου ·
traditions.KJV: one ] would think the deep [ to be ] hoary .

traditions.VUL: Non est super terram potéstas , quæ comparétur ei ,

traditions.KJV: who is made without fear .
He beholdeth all high [ things ] :

traditions.KJV: he [ is ] a king over all the children of pride .
